summary: Baileys Harbor range lights, Door County, Wisconsin: two wooden lights built in 1869 and lit in 1870 to steer ships into the harbor; electrified 1930.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NRHP nomination dates Sweet's harbor light to 1851 and LighthouseFriends to 1853 operation; both predate the range lights, which were built in 1869 and first lit in 1870.
The fiscal 1897 Light-House Board repairs list says the steamer lens was replaced; the changes list says the light was changed from a sixth-order to a reflector light. Story reports both.
LighthouseFriends 1895, Light-House Board fiscal 1896, NRHP about 1900. Story gives the range of sources in the fact row.

notes_for_editor: (1) USLHS lists no keepers for the Front light; the eight keeper lines are the archive's Rear record (where the keeper lived). Person slugs are on those lines, so the keepers index will join them to this station too: check against us-wi-baileys-harbor-range-rear to avoid double rows. (2) The 1897 front-light change conflicts: the Light-House Board's repairs list says a steamer lens was replaced by a fifth-order tubular burner; its changes list says a sixth-order lens was changed to a reflector; LighthouseFriends says a steamer lens. (3) Focal heights conflict: NRHP gives 39 ft for the rear and 22 ft for the front; USLHS gives a 22 ft focal height for the rear; the record's 21.0 m focal height matches neither. (4) Light-House Board page numbers come from the volume's index and its scan pages; the printed page 14 for the changes list is not read from the image. (5) The Chronicling America search (WI, 1869-1930, 'Baileys Harbor' with 'lighthouse') returned no page about the lights. (6) LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: only facts are used, with at most a few words quoted. (7) Fact-check 2026-10-22: each quote re-checked against the cached NRHP nomination, LighthouseFriends page and the Light-House Board volume. Board pages confirmed by OCR: the 1896 oil-house and sidewalk entry is printed p. 121 (scan 145); the 1897 front-light lens entry is p. 135 (scan 395); the 1897 changes list is in the 1897 report (scan 264, printed page not read). (8) The NRHP listing event (1989) was removed: the cached nomination does not state a listing date. (9) Not reconciled: the NRHP gives a fifth-order burner for the front light in 1897, and LighthouseFriends shows a sixth-order lens from the front tower on display; the story reports both attributions. (10) LighthouseFriends says kerosene was used from 1880; the story keeps its lard-oil statement for the early years and does not date the change. (11) The USLHS front record lists no keepers in the cached copy; the People link (showPeople/9528) returned no names.
